characterization_methods.technique: Spin-polarized total and partial density of states (TDOS/PDOS)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Covalent and metallic bonding coexist; electrons localized around Fe, Mn and Al atoms indicate covalent bonds, while delocalized electrons indicate metallic bonding.
characterization_methods.technique: Total electron density distribution and electron density difference maps

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 8x8x8 Monkhorst-Pack k-point mesh; 450 eV plane-wave cutoff energy; total energy converged to 2x10^-6 eV; forces reduced below 0.5 eV·nm⁻¹; cubic supercell (space group Pm-3m) with Mn substituting Fe on the Fe sublattice.
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: GGA-PBE exchange-correlation; ultrasoft pseudopotentials; valence electron states Fe 3d6 4s2, Mn 3d5 4s2, Al 3s2 3p1
computational_details.simulation_method: Density functional theory (DFT) first-principles calculation, plane-wave pseudopotential method
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameters and results show good agreement with other experimental and calculated values; slight deviations attributed to differences in calculation methods and experimental conditions.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Computational geometry optimization of the Fe0.5Mn0.5Al cubic supercell via first-principles DFT; no experimental thermal or mechanical processing was applied.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: DFT-calculated (CASTEP, GGA-PBE) values at equilibrium geometry; no experimental test conditions.

phases_present.crystal_structure: cubic (B2-type, space group Pm-3m), a = b = c = 0.578 nm

structures.overall_structure: B2-type cubic supercell (space group Pm-3m) derived from FeAl by substituting Mn for Fe on the Fe sublattice; 16-atom cell with 8 Al sites and 8 Fe/Mn sites (4 Fe + 4 Mn for Fe0.5Mn0.5Al). Optimized lattice parameter a = b = c = 0.578 nm.

unmapped_findings: Optimized cubic lattice parameter for Fe0.5Mn0.5Al: a = b = c = 0.578 nm (Table 1).
Thermodynamic stability: cohesive energy E_coh = -6.843 eV·atom⁻¹ and formation enthalpy ΔH_r = -0.334 eV·atom⁻¹ (Table 1); both negative, indicating thermal stability.
Elastic constants (Table 2): C11 = 225.0 GPa, C12 = 152.0 GPa, C44 = 126.2 GPa. Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the lowest C11 and C44 and the highest C12 among the Fe-containing Fe1-xMnxAl compounds.
Elastic moduli (Table 2): bulk modulus B = 176.3 GPa, shear modulus G = 77.2 GPa, Poisson's ratio σ = 0.309, B/G = 2.28 (dimensionless). B/G > 1.75 indicates ductile behavior.

Anisotropy (Table 3): universal anisotropic index A^U = 2.06, A_B = 0, A_G = 0.171, shear anisotropic factors A1 = A2 = A3 = 3.46. Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the largest A^U among the Fe-containing compounds (strongest elastic anisotropy among them).

Bonding/metallic character: Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the highest B/G ratio (2.28) and lowest Debye temperature (533.3 K) among the Fe-containing Fe1-xMnxAl compounds, indicating the strongest metallic character and weakest covalent bonds among them (Table 4 and text b0075).

Text statement (b0047): Fe0.5Mn0.5Al has the lowest C11 (225.0 GPa), maximum C12, minimum C44, minimum E (202.1 GPa) and maximum Poisson's ratio, which the text describes as the highest hardness and best ductility among the Fe1-xMnxAl compounds (note: Table 2 lists its H_V = 6.7 GPa, the lowest hardness value among the Fe-containing alloys).
